problem_text: Let k be a field, X and Y indeterminates, and suppose that α is a positive irrational number. Show the map v: k[X,Y] → ℝ∪{∞} defined by v(∑ c_{n,m} X^n Y^m) = min{n + mα | c_{n,m} ≠ 0} determines a valuation of k(X,Y) with value group ℤ + ℤα.
solution_text: Proof: (1) v is well-defined: for nonzero f, the set {n+mα | c_{n,m}≠0} is finite so min exists; v(0)=∞. (2) v(f+g) ≥ min(v(f),v(g)): support of f+g ⊆ support(f) ∪ support(g), so each term weight ≥ min(v(f),v(g)). (3) v(fg)=v(f)+v(g): Let f's min-weight term be c_{n₀,m₀}X^{n₀}Y^{m₀} (weight w_f) and g's be d_{p₀,q₀}X^{p₀}Y^{q₀} (weight w_g). Any term in fg has weight (n+mα)+(p+qα) ≥ w_f+w_g. Equality iff (n,m)=(n₀,m₀) and (p,q)=(p₀,q₀), by irrationality of α (n₁-n₂=(m₂-m₁)α implies n₁=n₂,m₁=m₂). The min-weight term in fg has coefficient c_{n₀,m₀}d_{p₀,q₀}≠0 (field). So v(fg)=w_f+w_g. (4) Extension: v extends uniquely to k(X,Y) by v(f/g)=v(f)-v(g). (5) Value group: values on k[X,Y] are {n+mα | n,m∈ℤ≥0}, on k(X,Y) are {n+mα | n,m∈ℤ}=ℤ+ℤα.
solution_summary: Verify v satisfies valuation axioms on k[X,Y]: well-definedness (finite min), triangle inequality (support containment), and multiplicativity (irrationality of α ensures unique minimum weight term so no cancellation in products). Then extend to fraction field k(X,Y) and identify value group as ℤ+ℤα.
answer: v determines a valuation of k(X,Y) with value group ℤ + ℤα
structure_features: Map from polynomial ring to ordered group; verify valuation axioms; irrationality hypothesis is the key structural ingredient that ensures uniqueness of minimum weight term in products
key_insight: Irrationality of α ensures that n₁+m₁α = n₂+m₂α implies (n₁,m₁)=(n₂,m₂), so the minimum weight term in a product is unique and its coefficient is nonzero — this makes v multiplicative
translation_from: direct minimum computation on polynomial coefficients
translation_to: valuation-theoretic argument using irrationality for uniqueness
expected_ai_method: Direct calculation: verify each valuation axiom by computing minima over supports, without recognizing the role of irrationality in preventing cancellation
correct_method: Use irrationality of α to prove uniqueness of minimum weight term, establishing multiplicativity; then extend valuation from integral domain to fraction field

tell_hint_pairs.hint: You're right to worry about cancellation. How many terms in the product can have the minimum weight w_f + w_g? Use the irrationality of α to count them

tell_hint_pairs.hint: If n₁+m₁α = n₂+m₂α, then n₁-n₂ = (m₂-m₁)α. Since α is irrational, the only solution is n₁=n₂ and m₁=m₂. So the minimum weight term is unique — no cancellation possible

tell_hint_pairs.hint: A valuation on an integral domain extends uniquely to its fraction field by v(f/g)=v(f)-v(g). What values does v take? The value group is generated by 1 and α

tell_hint_pairs.tell: AI has all components: well-definedness, axioms, extension, value group — needs to assemble the complete argument
tell_hint_pairs.hint: Put it all together: v is well-defined, satisfies all valuation axioms (multiplicativity via irrationality), extends to k(X,Y), and has value group ℤ+ℤα. The proof is complete

global_tell_hint_pairs.hint: Irrationality of α is not a side condition but the central structural ingredient: it ensures n+mα gives distinct values for distinct (n,m) pairs, making the minimum weight term in any product unique and nonzero

Only when viewing the complete proof path does it become clear that irrationality is the single hypothesis that makes the entire valuation structure work — without it, multiplicativity fails and v is not a valuation

global_tell_hint_pairs.hint: The value group ℤ+ℤα is not just a byproduct but characterizes the valuation as a monomial weight valuation: the two generators 1 and α correspond to the weights of X and Y respectively, and irrationality ensures they are linearly independent over ℤ
global_tell_hint_pairs.generalizability: medium — the connection between value group structure and weight assignments generalizes to other monomial valuations, but the specific rank-2 structure is particular to this two-variable setting

bare_ai_error_prediction: Bare AI will likely verify the additive axiom and well-definedness correctly, but will struggle with multiplicativity: it may attempt direct computation without recognizing that irrationality prevents cancellation, or may incorrectly assume the minimum is always achieved by a unique term without justifying why. It may also fail to extend the valuation from k[X,Y] to k(X,Y).

rounds.question: Describe the problem structure: what is v, what are the valuation axioms, and what role might the irrationality of α play?
rounds.expected_answer: v maps polynomials to ℝ∪{∞} by taking min of n+mα over nonzero terms. Valuation axioms: v(fg)=v(f)+v(g), v(f+g)≥min(v(f),v(g)), v(0)=∞. Irrationality of α likely matters for uniqueness of the minimum.

rounds.question: Among the three axioms, which one would fail if α were rational? Think about what could go wrong with v(fg)=v(f)+v(g).
rounds.expected_answer: If α were rational, say α=p/q, then n₁+m₁α could equal n₂+m₂α for different (n₁,m₁)≠(n₂,m₂). This means multiple terms in a product could have the same minimum weight and cancel, making v(fg) > v(f)+v(g) possible. The additive axiom would still hold.

rounds.question: Prove v(f+g) ≥ min(v(f),v(g)). Then try v(fg)=v(f)+v(g): what happens when you multiply two polynomials and look at the minimum weight?
rounds.expected_answer: Additive: support(f+g) ⊆ support(f)∪support(g), so min weight of f+g ≥ min(min weight f, min weight g). For product: the minimum weight term should come from product of minimum weight terms, but need to check no cancellation.

rounds.question: You're worried about cancellation in the product. How many terms in fg can have the minimum weight w_f+w_g? Use the irrationality of α to count them.
rounds.expected_answer: A term c_{n,m}d_{p,q} in fg has weight (n+mα)+(p+qα). For this to equal w_f+w_g, need n+mα=w_f and p+qα=w_g. By irrationality, each equation has a unique solution, so only one term achieves the minimum weight — no cancellation possible.

rounds.question: Prove that n₁+m₁α = n₂+m₂α with α irrational implies n₁=n₂ and m₁=m₂. Conclude v(fg)=v(f)+v(g).
rounds.expected_answer: n₁-n₂ = (m₂-m₁)α. If m₂≠m₁, then α = (n₁-n₂)/(m₂-m₁) ∈ ℚ, contradiction. So m₁=m₂, hence n₁=n₂. The unique minimum weight term in fg has coefficient c_{n₀,m₀}d_{p₀,q₀}≠0 (field), so v(fg)=w_f+w_g=v(f)+v(g).

rounds.question: Extend v from k[X,Y] to k(X,Y) and identify the value group.
rounds.expected_answer: Since k[X,Y] is an integral domain and v is a valuation on it, v extends to k(X,Y) by v(f/g)=v(f)-v(g). Values on monomials are n+mα for n,m≥0; on k(X,Y) we get all n+mα for n,m∈ℤ, which is ℤ+ℤα.

rounds.question: Assemble the complete argument: v is well-defined, satisfies all valuation axioms, extends to k(X,Y), and has value group ℤ+ℤα.
rounds.expected_answer: Complete proof: (1) v well-defined (finite min). (2) v(f+g)≥min(v(f),v(g)) (support containment). (3) v(fg)=v(f)+v(g) (irrationality → unique min → no cancellation). (4) Extension to fraction field. (5) Value group = ℤ+ℤα. QED.
